newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland generator switches to gas on schedule.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland generator switches to gas on schedule.

text.p: The conversion to natural gas from fuel oil has proceeded on schedule at a Northern Ireland power generator near Belfast.
The first of six 200 megawatt generating units designed to burn gas came on stream on Monday at Premier Power's -- a unit of British Gas Plc -- Ballylunford power station.
"We are running at 60 percent capacity," said Premier Power's Sam Cunningham.
The facility took its first delivery of gas on October 1 via a 135 km pipeline from Dumfries and Galloway in southwest Scotland. A further 26 km stretch takes gas to Belfast.
The second of the six generating units will come on stream on October 18 followed by the third in early November. The remaining three will become active early next year.
It remains uncertain whether Premier Power will need to buy fuel in November as a stop-gap measure to cover any shortfall during the changeover.

Premier Power was one of Europe's largest end-users of high sulphur fuel oil, consuming around 900,000 tonnes a year out of a European total of 2.5 million tonnes and some dealers had predicted there would be a bearish impact from the swap to gas.

But, this has not occurred with fuel oil prices hovering around five year highs and product difficult to source. Dealers said the withdrawal was well publicised and the market has evolved over the last year, effectively diminishing the loss of business from Premier that at its peak amounted to three to four cargoes a month.
"Supply is not what it was 12 months ago," said a trader at a major. "We will have a thinner market, but still tight market."
